The ending feels natural and earned because it brings the central conflict and themes to a satisfying resolution. Throughout the story, Daniel is haunted by an unlived past with his ex-wife, Rachel, symbolized by the recurring dream of the empty apartment. By finding the physical keys, unlocking the forgotten memory of the apartment and the canoe trip, and then creating a new, parallel canoe memory with his current partner, Isabel, Daniel is finally able to integrate his past into his present without letting it become a "rival." His final dream shifts from being about Rachel to being an acknowledgment of his younger self, and the story concludes with him looking forward—inviting Isabel back to the river—showing that his character arc is complete and providing a strong sense of emotional closure.
